office.title: Indiana School Board Member
office.summary: A school board is the elected or appointed governing body of a public school corporation, the legal unit that runs a local school district [1, 2]. The board hires and evaluates the superintendent, adopts policies, and approves the annual budget, while the superintendent and staff run schools day to day [3]. Most boards have five or seven members serving staggered four-year terms [3]. Starting in 2026, candidates may list a political party, run as independents, or list no affiliation on the ballot, and there is no primary for these seats [2, 4].

facts.label: Term
facts.value: 4 years, with elections staggered so part of the board is chosen every two years [3]

facts.label: Elected
facts.value: At the November general election (November 3, 2026, or November 2028 for some seats); depending on the local organization plan, members represent the whole school corporation (at large) or a district within it, and some boards are wholly or partly appointed [2]

facts.label: Ballot label
facts.value: Each candidate chooses a party label, 'Independent', or no affiliation, shown next to the name; no primary and no straight-ticket voting for these races [2, 4]

facts.label: Pay
facts.value: Set by board resolution: an annual amount of no more than 10% of the lowest starting teacher salary in the school corporation, plus a capped per diem [5]

duties: Hires, evaluates and can dismiss the superintendent, and approves the hiring and firing of principals, teachers and other staff recommended by the superintendent [1, 7, 3].
Adopts the annual budget, appropriates funds and oversees school finances [1, 3].

Decides whether to ask voters to approve an operating referendum (an extra property tax levy); the board adopts the resolution and the Department of Local Government Finance reviews the ballot language for compliance with state law [8].
Approves contracts, buys and sells property, and decides on construction, repair and demolition of school buildings [1].

Bargains with the teachers' union over salary, wages and wage-related benefits such as health insurance and retirement; state law excludes teacher evaluation procedures from those bargaining subjects [9].
Writes and updates policies and rules for schools, often in a policy handbook, including the student handbook [1, 3].
Buys curricular materials, provides them to students without charge, and runs programs such as student transportation and school lunch [1].

Must adopt a process for parents and residents to ask that library material be removed as obscene or harmful to minors, review requests at public meetings and keep a public catalog of library materials [10].
Hears written appeals of student expulsions, unless the board has voted not to hear them [11].
Must take official action openly; Indiana's Open Door Law says public agencies' official action is to be conducted openly so the people may be fully informed [12, 13].

A school board member must have lived in the school corporation (and, for a district seat, the district) for at least one year before the election, and a teacher or other employee of the school corporation may not serve on its board [2].

What the board does not control: the State Board of Education adopts statewide academic standards [14], the General Assembly sets the state school funding formula in the state budget [15], and voucher (Choice Scholarship) eligibility is set by state law [16].
recent_changes: 2025: Senate Enrolled Act 287 allowed school board candidates to declare a party affiliation; the Indiana School Boards Association opposed the change, and a supporter quoted by WNDU, a Noblesville school board member, said it adds transparency [17].

2026: Candidates choose a party, 'Independent' or no affiliation on their nominating petition, and that choice appears on the ballot; a candidate claiming the Democratic or Republican party must have voted in that party's primary in the two most recent primaries they voted in, or have certification from the county party chair, or can be challenged and removed from the ballot [2].

July 2026: Chalkbeat reported, citing Indiana School Boards Association data, that 524 of 1,044 candidates chose a party, about 72% of them Republicans [18]; the Indiana Election Division's 2026 guidance and the wording of the law differ on the primary-voting test, a question county election boards decide [19].

February 2026: Senate Enrolled Act 25 set the order of school board candidates on the ballot, grouped by party, with candidates who list no affiliation placed after the party and independent candidates [20].

2025: Senate Enrolled Act 1, a property tax law, limits how much operating revenue districts can raise through taxes and restricts school referendums to statewide general elections in even-numbered years [21, 22].
2025: The same law requires districts to share operating revenue with brick-and-mortar charter schools that enroll their students, statewide starting in 2028 [21, 22].
2025: The state budget opened Choice Scholarship vouchers to all Indiana families starting in June 2026 [16].
2026: The Indianapolis Public Education Corporation, rather than the Indianapolis Public Schools board, now certifies Indianapolis Public Schools referendum questions for the ballot [20].

2023: Senate Enrolled Act 391 changed the so-called $1 law so the Indiana Department of Education can order districts that lost at least 10% of enrollment over five years to close schools under 60% capacity and offer them to charter schools [23].
2023: House Enrolled Act 1447 required school districts to set up procedures for complaints that library material is obscene or harmful to minors [10].

race_context: South Dearborn Community School Corporation (SDCSC) is based in Aurora in Dearborn County; after the 2025 closure of Manchester Elementary it runs four schools, including Aurora and Dillsboro elementaries, South Dearborn Middle School and South Dearborn High School [24, 25, 26]. State enrollment counts fell from 2,345 students in 2018-19 to 1,849 in 2024-25 and 1,822 in 2025-26 [27].

Superintendent: Dr. Janet Platt has been interim superintendent since Sept. 8, 2026, when the board approved a 'mutually agreeable separation agreement' with Superintendent Dr. Ronald Ross; the district said it would search for a permanent superintendent [28]. Platt attended her first board meeting as interim superintendent Sept. 15 [29].

The board has seven members; those listed at the Aug. 18, 2026 meeting were Jeff Lane, Steve Hamlett, Shawn Spindler, Scott Willoughby (president), Kelli Gentrup-Pettit, Daryl Cutter and Brandon Messmore [30]. Seats are elected on a staggered cycle: four members were elected in 2020 and 2024 and three in 2022 [31, 32, 33]. In 2012, Eagle Country described District 1 as Caesar Creek, Clay, Hogan and Washington townships, District 2 as Manchester and Sparta townships (two members elected that year) and District 3 as Center Township [34]; this guide did not confirm the current map.

Seats on the 2026 ballot: District 1, District 3 and At Large, one seat each, matching the state list's 'vote for 1' [6, 35]. These are the three seats filled in 2022 by Jeffery Allen Lane, Scott A. Willoughby and Amber L. Probst [32]. Lane (District 1) and Willoughby (District 3) are running again. Probst resigned in July 2025, and the board appointed Brandon Messmore to finish her term; he is running in the At Large race [36, 37, 38]. Every race is contested.
Party labels: 2026 is the first year Indiana school board candidates could list a party. Five of the six South Dearborn candidates filed as Republicans; Jeff Lane declared no party [38, 6].

Building closures (2025): the board voted 6-1 on April 15, 2025 to close Manchester Elementary, which had 140 students in a building designed for 400; the district projected savings of about $1 million and promised all staff positions elsewhere [39]. Ross cited declining enrollment, 'the loss of revenue stemming from Senate Bill 1' and costly capital needs at the building [24]. Moores Hill Elementary closed in 2021 [39]. In September 2026 the board approved selling the Manchester building [28]. Ross said in October 2025 that there were no plans to close Dillsboro Elementary [40].

Strategic plan (2025-26): the board approved strategic-plan goals including staff recruitment and retention and 'a clear, consistent district vision, curriculum and graduate profile,' and the district held public input sessions on a 'Profile of a Graduate' in January 2026 [26].

Leadership and transparency (Aug.-Sept. 2026): about 200 people attended the Aug. 18, 2026 board meeting, most to speak about a personnel action at Dillsboro Elementary, and some speakers blamed falling enrollment on the superintendent and board members [30]. An online petition calling for 'accountability, transparency, and leadership change' had nearly 300 signatures by Aug. 20 [41]. The board said it could not discuss personnel matters publicly; the matter was resolved Aug. 24, and on Sept. 8 the board approved the separation agreement with Ross [42, 43, 28].

Budget: apart from Ross's April 2025 reference to lost revenue from Senate Bill 1, this guide found no reporting on SDCSC's 2026 budget, any referendum plans or test-score and accountability results [24].

Forums: this guide found no 2026 candidate forum, questionnaire or campaign website for any South Dearborn candidate. The district website could not be loaded, and the Dearborn County Register's coverage is behind a paywall.

candidates.summary: Challenger for the District 1 seat held by Jeff Lane; listed as a Republican [6, 38].
background: The county's candidate list gives no occupation or other background, and this guide found no news coverage of the candidate [35].
path_to_ballot: Filed June 18, 2026 as a Republican, according to the state filing list as republished by The Indiana Citizen [38, 6].
gaps: This guide found no candidate website, social-media page, questionnaire, forum appearance or news interview for this candidate.
Occupation, residence within District 1 and ties to the schools are not reported.
No reporting found on this candidate's views on the 2025 property-tax law (SEA 1), school closures, the 2026 superintendent change or other board issues.
No endorsements or campaign-finance reports found.

candidates.summary: Incumbent; elected in 2022 and running for another term without a party designation [32, 30, 6].
background: A 'Jeffery Allen Lane' was elected to the South Dearborn board in November 2022 with 3,111 votes, one of three South Dearborn board members elected that year [32]. Lane was listed among the seven board members at the Aug. 18, 2026 meeting [30].
In 2012, a candidate named Jeffery Allen Lane ran for the District 1 seat (Caesar Creek, Clay, Hogan and Washington townships) against incumbent Daryl L. Cutter [34].
path_to_ballot: Filed June 12, 2026 without declaring a party; the state list shows him as Nonpartisan [38, 6].
on_incumbent: Is a current board member. He took part in the board's 6-1 vote of April 15, 2025 on Manchester Elementary, in its Aug. 2026 statements about a Dillsboro Elementary personnel matter and in the September 2026 superintendent change, but this guide found no statement from him about those decisions; Eagle Country did not report how individual members voted [39, 42, 28].
gaps: This guide found no candidate website, social-media page, questionnaire, forum appearance or news interview for this candidate.
Occupation and community roles are not reported.
How Lane voted on the Manchester Elementary closure (one member voted no) is not reported in sources read.
No endorsements or campaign-finance reports found.

candidates.summary: Incumbent and board president; elected in 2022 and running for another term as a Republican [32, 30, 6].
background: Elected to the board in November 2022 as 'Scott A Willoughby' with 3,073 votes [32]. He was board president at the Aug. 18, 2026 meeting [30].
on_incumbent: Is a current board member and the board's president. At the Aug. 18, 2026 meeting, where about 200 people came to speak about a Dillsboro Elementary personnel matter, he said the meeting would be extended if needed so everyone who wanted to speak could do so [30]. The board said in an Aug. 21 statement that it was 'continuing to gather information' and would 'make decisions based on the facts', and in September 2026 it approved a separation agreement with Superintendent Ron Ross and named an interim superintendent [42, 28]. This guide found no statement attributed to Willoughby personally on those decisions.
gaps: This guide found no candidate website, social-media page, questionnaire, forum appearance or news interview for this candidate.
Occupation and community roles are not reported.

A search-result snippet of a 2025 district notice suggested Willoughby was the contact for letters of interest when the board filled the 2025 vacancy; the district page could not be loaded to confirm this (unverified).
No endorsements or campaign-finance reports found.

background: The county's candidate list gives no occupation or other background, and this guide found no news coverage of the candidate [35].

candidates.summary: Appointed board member since August 2025, running for a full term as a Republican [37, 6].
background: Auto finance manager for the Mark Williams Group, with a career in automotive sales and management; graduate of East Central High School with a business communications degree from Northern Kentucky University, according to the district's announcement of his appointment [37].
Lives in Aurora, where he moved in 2011; parent of students in the district, including a recent South Dearborn graduate [37].

In April 2019, Eagle Country reported that parent Brandon Messmore spoke at a board work session on falling enrollment and facility needs, saying everybody had a reason to want South Dearborn's schools to succeed [44].
path_to_ballot: The board appointed him in August 2025 to serve the rest of the term of Amber Probst, who resigned in July 2025 for personal reasons [36, 37].
Filed May 19, 2026 as a Republican, the first of the six South Dearborn candidates to file [35, 38, 6].
on_incumbent: Is a current board member (appointed). On his appointment he said, 'South Dearborn offers so much to our kids, and I am committed to maintaining and growing those opportunities' [37]. He sat on the board during the August 2026 Dillsboro Elementary personnel matter and the September 2026 superintendent change; this guide found no statement from him personally on either [30, 28].
plans: At his appointment he said his goal was 'to help ensure every student has an enjoyable, fulfilling school experience that builds a strong foundation for lifelong success' [37].
gaps: No campaign website, questionnaire or forum appearance found.
Whether the At Large race is the same seat Messmore holds by appointment is inferred from the 2022 results and the appointment notice, not confirmed by the district.
No endorsements or campaign-finance reports found.
